HP:0000003.name: Multicystic kidney dysplasia
HP:0000003.definition: Multicystic dysplasia of the kidney is characterized by multiple cysts of varying size in the kidney and the absence of a normal pelvicaliceal system. The condition is associated with ureteral or ureteropelvic atresia, and the affected kidney is nonfunctional.

HP:0000014.name: Abnormality of the bladder
HP:0000014.definition: An abnormality of the urinary bladder.

HP:0000028.name: Cryptorchidism
HP:0000028.definition: Testis in inguinal canal. That is, absence of one or both testes from the scrotum owing to failure of the testis or testes to descend through the inguinal canal to the scrotum.

HP:0000044.name: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
HP:0000044.definition: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism is characterized by reduced function of the gonads (testes in males or ovaries in females) and results from the absence of the gonadal stimulating pituitary hormones: follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH).

HP:0000047.name: Hypospadias
HP:0000047.definition: Abnormal position of urethral meatus on the ventral penile shaft (underside) characterized by displacement of the urethral meatus from the tip of the glans penis to the ventral surface of the penis, scrotum, or perineum.

HP:0000053.name: Macroorchidism
HP:0000053.definition: The presence of abnormally large testes.

HP:0000054.name: Micropenis
HP:0000054.definition: Abnormally small penis. At birth, the normal penis is about 3 cm (stretched length from pubic tubercle to tip of penis) with micropenis less than 2.0-2.5 cm.

HP:0000062.name: Ambiguous genitalia
HP:0000062.definition: A genital phenotype that is not clearly assignable to a single gender. Ambiguous genitalia can be evaluated using the Prader scale: Prader 0: Normal female external genitalia. Prader 1: Female external genitalia with clitoromegaly. Prader 2: Clitoromegaly with partial labial fusion forming a funnel-shaped urogenital sinus. Prader 3: Increased phallic enlargement. Complete labioscrotal fusion forming a urogenital sinus with a single opening. Prader 4: Complete scrotal fusion with urogenital opening at the base or on the shaft of the phallus. Prader 5: Normal male external genitalia. The diagnosis of ambiguous genitalia is made for Prader 1-4.

HP:0000083.name: Renal insufficiency
HP:0000083.definition: A reduction in the level of performance of the kidneys in areas of function comprising the concentration of urine, removal of wastes, the maintenance of electrolyte balance, homeostasis of blood pressure, and calcium metabolism.

HP:0000090.name: Nephronophthisis
HP:0000090.definition: Presence of cysts at the corticomedullary junction of the kidney in combination with tubulointerstitial fibrosis.

HP:0000095.name: Abnormal renal glomerulus morphology
HP:0000095.definition: A structural anomaly of the glomerulus.
synonyms: Morphologic abnormality of the renal glomerulus

HP:0000100.name: Nephrotic syndrome
HP:0000100.definition: Nephrotic syndrome is a collection of findings resulting from glomerular dysfunction with an increase in glomerular capillary wall permeability associated with pronounced proteinuria. Nephrotic syndrome refers to the constellation of clinical findings that result from severe renal loss of protein, with Proteinuria and hypoalbuminemia, edema, and hyperlipidemia.

HP:0000105.name: Enlarged kidney
HP:0000105.definition: An abnormal increase in the size of the kidney.

HP:0000107.name: Renal cyst
HP:0000107.definition: A fluid filled sac in the kidney.

HP:0000110.name: Renal dysplasia
HP:0000110.definition: The presence of developmental dysplasia of the kidney.

HP:0000119.name: Abnormality of the genitourinary system
HP:0000119.definition: The presence of any abnormality of the genitourinary system.

HP:0000126.name: Hydronephrosis
HP:0000126.definition: Severe distention of the kidney with dilation of the renal pelvis and calices.

HP:0000133.name: Gonadal dysgenesis
HP:0000133.definition: Gonadal dysgenesis is the name given to any of a multitude of conditions that can cause impaired development of the gonads, i.e., the testes or ovaries, or to the related phenotypic features. The term is to be avoided if possible for new annotations, and more specific terms should be chosen.

HP:0000154.name: Wide mouth
HP:0000154.definition: Distance between the oral commissures more than 2 SD above the mean. Alternatively, an apparently increased width of the oral aperture (subjective).

HP:0000175.name: Cleft palate
HP:0000175.definition: Cleft palate is a developmental defect of the palate resulting from a failure of fusion of the palatine processes and manifesting as a separation of the roof of the mouth (soft and hard palate).
synonyms: Cleft of hard and soft palate

HP:0000190.name: Abnormal oral frenulum morphology
HP:0000190.definition: An abnormality of the lingual frenulum, that is of the small fold of mucous membrane that attaches the tongue to the floor of the mouth, or the presence of accessory frenula in the oral cavity.

HP:0000218.name: High palate
HP:0000218.definition: Height of the palate more than 2 SD above the mean (objective) or palatal height at the level of the first permanent molar more than twice the height of the teeth (subjective).

HP:0000219.name: Thin upper lip vermilion
HP:0000219.definition: Height of the vermilion of the upper lip in the midline more than 2 SD below the mean. Alternatively, an apparently reduced height of the vermilion of the upper lip in the frontal view (subjective).
synonyms: Decreased height of upper lip vermilion
Decreased volume of upper lip vermilion
Thin red part of the upper lip
Thin vermilion border of upper lip

HP:0000238.name: Hydrocephalus
HP:0000238.definition: Hydrocephalus is an active distension of the ventricular system of the brain resulting from inadequate passage of CSF from its point of production within the cerebral ventricles to its point of absorption into the systemic circulation.
synonyms: Too much cerebrospinal fluid in the brain

HP:0000252.name: Microcephaly
HP:0000252.definition: Head circumference below 2 standard deviations below the mean for age and gender.

HP:0000256.name: Macrocephaly
HP:0000256.definition: Occipitofrontal (head) circumference greater than 97th centile compared to appropriate, age matched, sex-matched normal standards. Alternatively, a apparently increased size of the cranium.

HP:0000272.name: Malar flattening
HP:0000272.definition: Underdevelopment of the malar prominence of the jugal bone (zygomatic bone in mammals), appreciated in profile, frontal view, and/or by palpation.

HP:0000277.name: Abnormal mandible morphology
HP:0000277.definition: Any abnormality of the mandible, the bone of the lower jaw.
synonyms: Abnormality of the lower jaw bone
Deformity of the lower jaw bone
Malformation of the lower jaw bone

HP:0000286.name: Epicanthus
HP:0000286.definition: A fold of skin starting above the medial aspect of the upper eyelid and arching downward to cover, pass in front of and lateral to the medial canthus.

HP:0000303.name: Mandibular prognathia
HP:0000303.definition: Abnormal prominence of the chin related to increased length of the mandible.

HP:0000316.name: Hypertelorism
HP:0000316.definition: Interpupillary distance more than 2 SD above the mean (alternatively, the appearance of an increased interpupillary distance or widely spaced eyes).

HP:0000324.name: Facial asymmetry
HP:0000324.definition: An abnormal difference between the left and right sides of the face.
synonyms: Asymmetry of right and left side of face

HP:0000327.name: Hypoplasia of the maxilla
HP:0000327.definition: Abnormally small dimension of the Maxilla. Usually creating a malocclusion or malalignment between the upper and lower teeth or resulting in a deficient amount of projection of the base of the nose and lower midface region.

HP:0000341.name: Narrow forehead
HP:0000341.definition: Width of the forehead or distance between the frontotemporales is more than two standard deviations below the mean (objective); or apparently narrow intertemporal region (subjective).

HP:0000343.name: Long philtrum
HP:0000343.definition: Distance between nasal base and midline upper lip vermilion border more than 2 SD above the mean. Alternatively, an apparently increased distance between nasal base and midline upper lip vermilion border.

HP:0000356.name: Abnormality of the outer ear
HP:0000356.definition: An abnormality of the external ear.

HP:0000403.name: Recurrent otitis media
HP:0000403.definition: Increased susceptibility to otitis media, as manifested by recurrent episodes of otitis media.

HP:0000405.name: Conductive hearing impairment
HP:0000405.definition: An abnormality of vibrational conductance of sound to the inner ear leading to impairment of sensory perception of sound.

HP:0000407.name: Sensorineural hearing impairment
HP:0000407.definition: A type of hearing impairment in one or both ears related to an abnormal functionality of the cochlear nerve.

HP:0000410.name: Mixed hearing impairment
HP:0000410.definition: A type of hearing loss resulting from a combination of conductive hearing impairment and sensorineural hearing impairment.

HP:0000453.name: Choanal atresia
HP:0000453.definition: Absence or abnormal closure of the choana (the posterior nasal aperture). Most embryologists believe that posterior choanal atresia results from a failure of rupture between the 35th and 38th day of fetal life of the partition which separates the bucconasal or buccopharyngeal membranes. The resultant choanal atresia may be unilateral or bilateral, bony or membranous, complete or incomplete. In over 90 per cent of cases the obstruction is bony, while in the remainder it is membranous. The bony type of atresia is commonly located 1-2 mm. anterior to the posterior edge of the hard palate, and the osseous septum varies in thickness from 1 to 10 mm. In the membranous form of choanal atresia the obstruction usually occurs further posteriorly. In approximately one third of cases the atresia is bilateral.
synonyms: Blockage of the rear opening of the nasal cavity

HP:0000458.name: Anosmia
HP:0000458.definition: An inability to perceive odors. This is a general term describing inability to smell arising in any part of the process of smelling from absorption of odorants into the nasal mucous overlying the olfactory epithelium, diffusion to the cilia, binding to olfactory receptor sites, generation of action potentials in olfactory neurons, and perception of a smell.

HP:0000465.name: Webbed neck
HP:0000465.definition: Pterygium colli is a congenital skin fold that runs along the sides of the neck down to the shoulders. It involves an ectopic fibrotic facial band superficial to the trapezius muscle. Excess hair-bearing skin is also present and extends down the cervical region well beyond the normal hairline.

HP:0000476.name: Cystic hygroma
HP:0000476.definition: A cystic lymphatic lesion of the neck.

HP:0000478.name: Abnormality of the eye
HP:0000478.definition: Any abnormality of the eye, including location, spacing, and intraocular abnormalities.

HP:0000486.name: Strabismus
HP:0000486.definition: A misalignment of the eyes so that the visual axes deviate from bifoveal fixation. The classification of strabismus may be based on a number of features including the relative position of the eyes, whether the deviation is latent or manifest, intermittent or constant, concomitant or otherwise and according to the age of onset and the relevance of any associated refractive error.

HP:0000496.name: Abnormality of eye movement
HP:0000496.definition: An abnormality in voluntary or involuntary eye movements or their control.
synonyms: Abnormal motility of the globe of the eye
Abnormal movement of the globe of the eye

HP:0000501.name: Glaucoma
HP:0000501.definition: Glaucoma refers loss of retinal ganglion cells in a characteristic pattern of optic neuropathy usually associated with increased intraocular pressure.

HP:0000505.name: Visual impairment
HP:0000505.definition: Visual impairment (or vision impairment) is vision loss (of a person) to such a degree as to qualify as an additional support need through a significant limitation of visual capability resulting from either disease, trauma, or congenital or degenerative conditions that cannot be corrected by conventional means, such as refractive correction, medication, or surgery.

HP:0000510.name: Rod-cone dystrophy
HP:0000510.definition: An inherited retinal disease subtype in which the rod photoreceptors appear to be more severely affected than the cone photoreceptors. Typical presentation is with nyctalopia (due to rod dysfunction) followed by loss of mid-peripheral field of vision, which gradually extends and leaves many patients with a small central island of vision due to the preservation of macular cones.

HP:0000512.name: Abnormal electroretinogram
HP:0000512.definition: Any abnormality of the electrical responses of various cell types in the retina as measured by electroretinography.

HP:0000518.name: Cataract
HP:0000518.definition: A cataract is an opacity or clouding that develops in the crystalline lens of the eye or in its capsule.
synonyms: Clouding of the lens of the eye

HP:0000525.name: Abnormality iris morphology
HP:0000525.definition: An abnormality of the iris, which is the pigmented muscular tissue between the cornea and the lens, that is perforated by an opening called the pupil.

HP:0000539.name: Abnormality of refraction
HP:0000539.definition: An abnormality in the process of focusing of light by the eye in order to produce a sharp image on the retina.

HP:0000556.name: Retinal dystrophy
HP:0000556.definition: Retinal dystrophy is an abnormality of the retina associated with a hereditary process. Retinal dystrophies are defined by their predominantly monogenic inheritance and they are frequently associated with loss or dysfunction of photoreceptor cells as a primary or secondary event.
synonyms: Breakdown of light-sensitive cells in back of eye

HP:0000568.name: Microphthalmia
HP:0000568.definition: A developmental anomaly characterized by abnormal smallness of one or both eyes.
synonyms: Decreased size of globe of eye

HP:0000589.name: Coloboma
HP:0000589.definition: A developmental defect characterized by a cleft of some portion of the eye or ocular adnexa.

HP:0000592.name: Blue sclerae
HP:0000592.definition: An abnormal bluish coloration of the sclera.
synonyms: Blue outer white part of eyeball
Whites of eyes are a bluish-gray color
Whites of eyes are a bluish-gray colour

HP:0000601.name: Hypotelorism
HP:0000601.definition: Interpupillary distance less than 2 SD below the mean (alternatively, the appearance of an decreased interpupillary distance or closely spaced eyes).

HP:0000613.name: Photophobia
HP:0000613.definition: Excessive sensitivity to light with the sensation of discomfort or pain in the eyes due to exposure to bright light.
synonyms: Extreme sensitivity of the eyes to light

HP:0000618.name: Blindness
HP:0000618.definition: Blindness is the condition of lacking visual perception defined as a profound reduction in visual perception. On the 6m visual acuity scale, blindness is defined as less than 3/60. On the 20ft visual acuity scale, blindness is defined as less than 20/400. On the decimal visual acuity scale, blindness is defined as less than 0.05. Blindness is typically characterized by a visual field of no greater than 10 degrees in radius around central fixation.

HP:0000639.name: Nystagmus
HP:0000639.definition: Rhythmic, involuntary oscillations of one or both eyes related to abnormality in fixation, conjugate gaze, or vestibular mechanisms.

HP:0000657.name: Oculomotor apraxia
HP:0000657.definition: Ocular motor apraxia is a deficiency in voluntary, horizontal, lateral, fast eye movements (saccades) with retention of slow pursuit movements. The inability to follow objects visually is often compensated by head movements. There may be decreased smooth pursuit, and cancelation of the vestibulo-ocular reflex.

HP:0000694.name: Odontodysplasia
HP:0000694.definition: The diagnosis odontodysplasia requires clinical and radiological exams, in which unusually large pulp chambers and large pulp room chambers with thin enamel and dentin are visible. It may affect either a single tooth or several teeth. The term regional odontodysplasia is used if several teeth are affected. It affects the deciduous and permanent dentitions in the maxilla, the mandible or both, although the maxilla is more frequently involved. A type of dental dysplasia occurring in dentinogenesis imperfecta in which the pulp chambers are enlarged and there is a reduced amount of coronal dentin.
synonyms: Teeth with thin dentin and large pulp chambers
Teeth with type iii dentinogenesis imperfecta

HP:0000707.name: Abnormality of the nervous system
HP:0000707.definition: An abnormality of the nervous system.

HP:0000708.name: Atypical behavior
HP:0000708.definition: Atypical behavior is an abnormality in a person's actions that can be controlled or modulated by the will of the individual. While abnormal behaviors can be difficult to control, they are distinct from other abnormal actions that cannot be affected by the individual's will.

HP:0000729.name: Autistic behavior
HP:0000729.definition: Persistent deficits in social interaction and communication and interaction as well as a markedly restricted repertoire of activity and interest as well as repetitive patterns of behavior.

HP:0000766.name: Abnormal sternum morphology
HP:0000766.definition: An anomaly of the sternum, also known as the breastbone.

HP:0000774.name: Narrow chest
HP:0000774.definition: Reduced width of the chest from side to side, associated with a reduced distance from the sternal notch to the tip of the shoulder.

HP:0000776.name: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia
HP:0000776.definition: The presence of a hernia of the diaphragm present at birth.

HP:0000787.name: Kidney stone
HP:0000787.definition: Kidney stones (calculi) are mineral concretions in the renal calyces and pelvis that are found free or attached to the renal papillae.

HP:0000790.name: Hematuria
HP:0000790.definition: The presence of blood in the urine. Hematuria may be gross hematuria (visible to the naked eye) or microscopic hematuria (detected by dipstick or microscopic examination of the urine).

HP:0000818.name: Abnormality of the endocrine system
HP:0000818.definition: An abnormality of the endocrine system.

HP:0000819.name: Diabetes mellitus
HP:0000819.definition: A group of abnormalities characterized by hyperglycemia and glucose intolerance.

HP:0000822.name: Hypertension
HP:0000822.definition: The presence of chronic increased pressure in the systemic arterial system.

HP:0000823.name: Delayed puberty
HP:0000823.definition: Passing the age when puberty normally occurs with no physical or hormonal signs of the onset of puberty.

HP:0000824.name: Decreased response to growth hormone stimulation test
HP:0000824.definition: Insufficient responses to growth hormone (GH) provocation tests. GH deficiency is defined as a serum peak GH concentration less than 10 ng/mL on provocation with a combination of at least two separate stimulation tests.

HP:0000836.name: Hyperthyroidism
HP:0000836.definition: An abnormality of thyroid physiology characterized by excessive secretion of the thyroid hormones thyroxine (i.e., T4) and/or 3,3',5-triiodo-L-thyronine zwitterion (i.e., triiodothyronine or T3).

HP:0000846.name: Adrenal insufficiency
HP:0000846.definition: Insufficient production of steroid hormones (primarily cortisol) by the adrenal glands.

HP:0000871.name: Panhypopituitarism
HP:0000871.definition: A pituitary functional deficit affecting all the anterior pituitary hormones (growth hormone, thyroid-stimulating hormone, follicle-stimulating hormone, luteinizing hormone, adrenocorticotropic hormone, and prolactin).

HP:0000889.name: Abnormal clavicle morphology
HP:0000889.definition: Any abnormality of the clavicles (collar bones).

HP:0000924.name: Abnormality of the skeletal system
HP:0000924.definition: An abnormality of the skeletal system.

HP:0000925.name: Abnormality of the vertebral column
HP:0000925.definition: Any abnormality of the vertebral column.

HP:0000938.name: Osteopenia
HP:0000938.definition: Osteopenia is a term to define bone density that is not normal but also not as low as osteoporosis. By definition from the World Health Organization osteopenia is defined by bone densitometry as a T score -1 to -2.5.

HP:0000944.name: Abnormal metaphysis morphology
HP:0000944.definition: An abnormality of one or more metaphysis, i.e., of the somewhat wider portion of a long bone that is adjacent to the epiphyseal growth plate and grows during childhood.
synonyms: Abnormality of the wide portion of a long bone

HP:0000956.name: Acanthosis nigricans
HP:0000956.definition: A dermatosis characterized by thickened, hyperpigmented plaques, typically on the intertriginous surfaces and neck.

HP:0000992.name: Cutaneous photosensitivity
HP:0000992.definition: An increased sensitivity of the skin to light. Photosensitivity may result in a rash upon exposure to the sun (which is known as photodermatosis). Photosensitivity can be diagnosed by phototests in which light is shone on small areas of skin.

HP:0001004.name: Lymphedema
HP:0001004.definition: Localized fluid retention and tissue swelling caused by a compromised lymphatic system.
synonyms: Swelling caused by excess lymph fluid under skin

HP:0001007.name: Hirsutism
HP:0001007.definition: Abnormally increased hair growth referring to a male pattern of body hair (androgenic hair).

HP:0001047.name: Atopic dermatitis
HP:0001047.definition: Atopic dermatitis (AD) or atopic eczema is an itchy, inflammatory skin condition with a predilection for the skin flexures. It is characterized by poorly defined erythema with edema, vesicles, and weeping in the acute stage and skin thickening (lichenification) in the chronic stage.

HP:0001062.name: Atypical nevus
HP:0001062.definition: A large pigmented lesion measuring 5-15 mm in diameter with irregular, notched, and ill defined border and with color that may range from tan to dark brown to pink.

HP:0001081.name: Cholelithiasis
HP:0001081.definition: Hard, pebble-like deposits that form within the gallbladder.

HP:0001123.name: Visual field defect
synonyms: Partial loss of field of vision

HP:0001155.name: Abnormality of the hand
HP:0001155.definition: An abnormality affecting one or both hands.

HP:0001156.name: Brachydactyly
HP:0001156.definition: Digits that appear disproportionately short compared to the hand/foot. The word brachydactyly is used here to describe a series distinct patterns of shortened digits (brachydactyly types A-E). This is the sense used here.

HP:0001159.name: Syndactyly
HP:0001159.definition: Webbing or fusion of the fingers or toes, involving soft parts only or including bone structure. Bony fusions are referred to as "bony" syndactyly if the fusion occurs in a radio-ulnar axis. Fusions of bones of the fingers or toes in a proximo-distal axis are referred to as "symphalangism".

HP:0001162.name: Postaxial hand polydactyly
HP:0001162.definition: Supernumerary digits located at the ulnar side of the hand (that is, on the side with the fifth finger).

HP:0001166.name: Arachnodactyly
HP:0001166.definition: Abnormally long and slender fingers (spider fingers).

HP:0001171.name: Split hand
HP:0001171.definition: A condition in which middle parts of the hand (fingers and metacarpals) are missing giving a cleft appearance. The severity is very variable ranging from slightly hypoplastic middle fingers over absent middle fingers as far as oligo- or monodactyl hands.

HP:0001217.name: Clubbing
HP:0001217.definition: Broadening of the soft tissues (non-edematous swelling of soft tissues) of the digital tips in all dimensions associated with an increased longitudinal and lateral curvature of the nails.

HP:0001249.name: Intellectual disability
HP:0001249.definition: The term intellectual disability or intellectual developmental disorder is used to describe significantly sub-average intellectual and adaptive functioning based on clinical assessment and as measured by individually administered, appropriately normed, standardized and validated tests of intellectual functioning and adaptive behavior, with onset during the developmental period from infancy through adolescence.

HP:0001250.name: Seizure
HP:0001250.definition: A seizure is an intermittent abnormality of nervous system physiology characterized by a transient occurrence of signs and/or symptoms due to abnormal excessive or synchronous neuronal activity in the brain.

HP:0001251.name: Ataxia
HP:0001251.definition: Ataxia refers to impaired coordination of voluntary muscle movement. Cerebellar ataxia refers to ataxia due to dysfunction of the cerebellum. This causes a variety of elementary neurological deficits including asynergy (lack of coordination between muscles, limbs and joints), dysmetria (lack of ability to judge distances that can lead to under- or overshoot in grasping movements), and dysdiadochokinesia (inability to perform rapid movements requiring antagonizing muscle groups to be switched on and off repeatedly).

HP:0001252.name: Hypotonia
HP:0001252.definition: Hypotonia is an abnormally low muscle tone (the amount of tension or resistance to movement in a muscle). Even when relaxed, muscles have a continuous and passive partial contraction which provides some resistance to passive stretching. Hypotonia thus manifests as diminished resistance to passive stretching. Hypotonia is not the same as muscle weakness, although the two conditions can co-exist.

HP:0001263.name: Global developmental delay
HP:0001263.definition: A delay in the achievement of motor or mental milestones in the domains of development of a child, including motor skills, speech and language, cognitive skills, and social and emotional skills. This term should only be used to describe children younger than five years of age.

HP:0001276.name: Hypertonia
HP:0001276.definition: A condition in which there is increased muscle tone so that arms or legs, for example, are stiff and difficult to move.

HP:0001283.name: Bulbar palsy
HP:0001283.definition: Bulbar weakness (or bulbar palsy) refers to bilateral impairment of function of the lower cranial nerves IX, X, XI and XII, which occurs due to lower motor neuron lesion either at nuclear or fascicular level in the medulla or from bilateral lesions of the lower cranial nerves outside the brain-stem. Bulbar weakness is often associated with difficulty in chewing, weakness of the facial muscles, dysarthria, palatal weakness and regurgitation of fluids, dysphagia, and dysphonia.

HP:0001284.name: Areflexia
HP:0001284.definition: Absence of neurologic reflexes such as the knee-jerk reaction.

HP:0001305.name: Dandy-Walker malformation
HP:0001305.definition: A congenital brain malformation typically characterized by incomplete formation of the cerebellar vermis, dilation of the fourth ventricle, and enlargement of the posterior fossa. In layman's terms, Dandy Walker malformation is a cyst in the cerebellum (typically symmetrical) that is involved with the fourth ventricle. This may interfere with the ability to drain cerebrospinal fluid from the brain, resulting in hydrocephalus. Dandy Walker cysts are formed during early embryonic development, while the brain forms. The cyst in the cerebellum typically has several blood vessels running through it connecting to the brain, thereby prohibiting surgical removal.

HP:0001320.name: Cerebellar vermis hypoplasia
HP:0001320.definition: Underdevelopment of the vermis of cerebellum.

HP:0001321.name: Cerebellar hypoplasia
HP:0001321.definition: Cerebellar hypoplasia is a descriptive term implying a cerebellum with a reduced volume, but a normal shape and is stable over time.

HP:0001331.name: Absent septum pellucidum
HP:0001331.definition: Absence of the septum pellucidum (meaning translucent wall in Latin - SP), also known as the ventricle of Sylvius. The septum pellucidum is a thin, triangular double membrane separating the frontal horns of the right and left lateral ventricles of the brain. It extends between the anterior portion of the corpus callosum, and the body of the fornix and its width varies from 1.5 to 3.0 mm.

HP:0001337.name: Tremor
HP:0001337.definition: An unintentional, oscillating to-and-fro muscle movement about a joint axis.

HP:0001339.name: Lissencephaly
HP:0001339.definition: A spectrum of malformations of cortical development caused by insufficient neuronal migration that subsumes the terms agyria, pachygyria and subcortical band heterotopia. See also neuropathological definitions for 2-, 3-, and 4-layered lissencephaly.
synonyms: Fewer or absent grooves in brain

HP:0001347.name: Hyperreflexia
HP:0001347.definition: Hyperreflexia is the presence of hyperactive stretch reflexes of the muscles.

HP:0001360.name: Holoprosencephaly
HP:0001360.definition: Holoprosencephaly is a structural anomaly of the brain in which the developing forebrain fails to divide into two separate hemispheres and ventricles.

HP:0001363.name: Craniosynostosis
HP:0001363.definition: Craniosynostosis refers to the premature closure of the cranial sutures. Primary craniosynostosis refers to the closure of one or more sutures due to abnormalities in skull development, and secondary craniosynostosis results from failure of brain growth.

HP:0001395.name: Hepatic fibrosis
HP:0001395.definition: The presence of excessive fibrous connective tissue in the liver. Fibrosis is a reparative or reactive process.

HP:0001396.name: Cholestasis
HP:0001396.definition: Impairment of bile flow due to obstruction in bile ducts.
synonyms: Slowed or blocked flow of bile from liver

HP:0001409.name: Portal hypertension
HP:0001409.definition: Increased pressure in the portal vein.

HP:0001508.name: Failure to thrive
HP:0001508.definition: Failure to thrive (FTT) refers to a child whose physical growth is substantially below the norm.

HP:0001513.name: Obesity
HP:0001513.definition: Accumulation of substantial excess body fat.

HP:0001541.name: Ascites
HP:0001541.definition: Accumulation of fluid in the peritoneal cavity (between the layers of the peritoneum that lines the abdomen).
synonyms: Accumulation of fluid in the abdomen

HP:0001561.name: Polyhydramnios
HP:0001561.definition: The presence of excess amniotic fluid in the uterus during pregnancy.

HP:0001562.name: Oligohydramnios
HP:0001562.definition: Diminished amniotic fluid volume in pregnancy.

HP:0001596.name: Alopecia
HP:0001596.definition: A noncongenital process of hair loss, which may progress to partial or complete baldness.

HP:0001626.name: Abnormality of the cardiovascular system
HP:0001626.definition: Any abnormality of the cardiovascular system.

HP:0001627.name: Abnormal heart morphology
HP:0001627.definition: Any structural anomaly of the heart.

HP:0001629.name: Ventricular septal defect
HP:0001629.definition: A hole between the two bottom chambers (ventricles) of the heart. The defect is centered around the most superior aspect of the ventricular septum.
synonyms: Hole in heart wall separating two lower heart chambers

HP:0001631.name: Atrial septal defect
HP:0001631.definition: Atrial septal defect (ASD) is a congenital abnormality of the interatrial septum that enables blood flow between the left and right atria via the interatrial septum.
synonyms: An opening in the wall separating the top two chambers of the heart
Hole in heart wall separating two upper heart chambers

HP:0001635.name: Congestive heart failure
HP:0001635.definition: The presence of an abnormality of cardiac function that is responsible for the failure of the heart to pump blood at a rate that is commensurate with the needs of the tissues or a state in which abnormally elevated filling pressures are required for the heart to do so. Heart failure is frequently related to a defect in myocardial contraction.

HP:0001636.name: Tetralogy of Fallot
HP:0001636.definition: A congenital cardiac malformation comprising pulmonary stenosis, overriding aorta, ventricular septum defect, and right ventricular hypertrophy. The diagnosis of TOF is made if at least three of the four above mentioned features are present.

HP:0001638.name: Cardiomyopathy
HP:0001638.definition: A myocardial disorder in which the heart muscle is structurally and functionally abnormal, in the absence of coronary artery disease, hypertension, valvular disease and congenital heart disease sufficient to cause the observed myocardial abnormality.

HP:0001640.name: Cardiomegaly
HP:0001640.definition: Increased size of the heart, clinically defined as an increased transverse diameter of the cardiac silhouette that is greater than or equal to 50% of the transverse diameter of the chest (increased cardiothoracic ratio) on a posterior-anterior projection of a chest radiograph or a computed tomography.

HP:0001642.name: Pulmonic stenosis
HP:0001642.definition: A narrowing of the right ventricular outflow tract that can occur at the pulmonary valve (valvular stenosis), below the pulmonary valve (infundibular stenosis), or above the pulmonary valve (supravalvar stenosis).

HP:0001651.name: Dextrocardia
HP:0001651.definition: The heart is located in the right hand sided hemithorax. That is, there is a left-right reversal (or "mirror reflection") of the anatomical location of the heart in which the heart is locate on the right side instead of the left.
synonyms: Heart tip and four chambers point towards right side of body

HP:0001654.name: Abnormal heart valve morphology
HP:0001654.definition: Any structural abnormality of a cardiac valve.

HP:0001671.name: Abnormal cardiac septum morphology
HP:0001671.definition: An anomaly of the intra-atrial or intraventricular septum.

HP:0001674.name: Complete atrioventricular canal defect
HP:0001674.definition: A congenital heart defect characterized by a specific combination of heart defects with a common atrioventricular valve, primum atrial septal defect and inlet ventricular septal defect.

HP:0001680.name: Coarctation of aorta
HP:0001680.definition: Coarctation of the aorta is a narrowing or constriction of a segment of the aorta.

HP:0001696.name: Situs inversus totalis
HP:0001696.definition: A left-right reversal (or mirror reflection) of the anatomical location of the major thoracic and abdominal organs.
synonyms: All organs on wrong side of body

HP:0001697.name: Abnormal pericardium morphology
HP:0001697.definition: An abnormality of the pericardium, i.e., of the fluid filled sac that surrounds the heart and the proximal ends of the aorta, vena cava, and the pulmonary artery.

HP:0001702.name: Abnormal tricuspid valve morphology
HP:0001702.definition: Any structural anomaly of the tricuspid valve.

HP:0001733.name: Pancreatitis
HP:0001733.definition: The presence of inflammation in the pancreas.

HP:0001738.name: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency
HP:0001738.definition: Impaired function of the exocrine pancreas associated with a reduced ability to digest foods because of lack of digestive enzymes.
synonyms: Inability to properly digest food due to lack of pancreatic digestive enzymes

HP:0001744.name: Splenomegaly
HP:0001744.definition: Abnormal increased size of the spleen.

HP:0001762.name: Talipes equinovarus
HP:0001762.definition: Talipes equinovarus (also called clubfoot) typically has four main components: inversion and adduction of the forefoot; inversion of the heel and hindfoot; equinus (limitation of extension) of the ankle and subtalar joint; and internal rotation of the leg.

HP:0001789.name: Hydrops fetalis
HP:0001789.definition: The abnormal accumulation of fluid in two or more fetal compartments, including ascites, pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, and skin edema.

HP:0001871.name: Abnormality of blood and blood-forming tissues
HP:0001871.definition: An abnormality of the hematopoietic system.
synonyms: Abnormality of blood and blood-forming tissues

HP:0001873.name: Thrombocytopenia
HP:0001873.definition: A reduction in the number of circulating thrombocytes.

HP:0001903.name: Anemia
HP:0001903.definition: A reduction in erythrocytes volume or hemoglobin concentration.
synonyms: Low number of red blood cells or haemoglobin
Low number of red blood cells or hemoglobin

HP:0001923.name: Reticulocytosis
HP:0001923.definition: An elevation in the number of reticulocytes (immature erythrocytes) in the peripheral blood circulation.
synonyms: Increased number of immature red blood cells

HP:0001943.name: Hypoglycemia
HP:0001943.definition: A decreased concentration of glucose in the blood.

HP:0001947.name: Renal tubular acidosis
HP:0001947.definition: Acidosis owing to malfunction of the kidney tubules with accumulation of metabolic acids and hyperchloremia, potentially leading to complications including hypokalemia, hypercalcinuria, nephrolithiasis and nephrocalcinosis.
synonyms: Accumulation of acid in body due to kidney problem

HP:0001954.name: Recurrent fever
HP:0001954.definition: Periodic (episodic or recurrent) bouts of fever.

HP:0001970.name: Tubulointerstitial nephritis
HP:0001970.definition: A form of inflammation of the kidney affecting the interstitium of the kidneys surrounding the tubules.

HP:0001987.name: Hyperammonemia
HP:0001987.definition: An increased concentration of ammonia in the blood.

HP:0001999.name: Abnormal facial shape
HP:0001999.definition: An abnormal morphology (form) of the face or its components.

HP:0002007.name: Frontal bossing
HP:0002007.definition: Bilateral bulging of the lateral frontal bone prominences with relative sparing of the midline.

HP:0002013.name: Vomiting
HP:0002013.definition: Forceful ejection of the contents of the stomach through the mouth by means of a series of involuntary spasmic contractions.

HP:0002023.name: Anal atresia
HP:0002023.definition: Congenital absence of the anus, i.e., the opening at the bottom end of the intestinal tract.

HP:0002031.name: Abnormal esophagus morphology
HP:0002031.definition: A structural abnormality of the esophagus.

HP:0002059.name: Cerebral atrophy
HP:0002059.definition: Atrophy (wasting, decrease in size of cells or tissue) affecting the cerebrum.

HP:0002076.name: Migraine
HP:0002076.definition: Migraine is a chronic neurological disorder characterized by episodic attacks of headache and associated symptoms.

HP:0002086.name: Abnormality of the respiratory system
HP:0002086.definition: An abnormality of the respiratory system, which include the airways, lungs, and the respiratory muscles.

HP:0002088.name: Abnormal lung morphology
HP:0002088.definition: Any structural anomaly of the lung.

HP:0002092.name: Pulmonary arterial hypertension
HP:0002092.definition: Pulmonary hypertension is defined mean pulmonary artery pressure of 25mmHg or more and pulmonary capillary wedge pressure of 15mmHg or less when measured by right heart catheterisation at rest and in a supine position.
synonyms: Increased blood pressure in blood vessels of lungs

HP:0002094.name: Dyspnea
HP:0002094.definition: Difficult or labored breathing. Dyspnea is a subjective feeling only the patient can rate, e.g., on a Borg scale.

HP:0002098.name: Respiratory distress
HP:0002098.definition: Respiratory distress is objectively observable as the physical or emotional consequences from the experience of dyspnea. The physical presentation of respiratory distress is generally referred to as labored breathing, while the sensation of respiratory distress is called shortness of breath or dyspnea.

HP:0002099.name: Asthma
HP:0002099.definition: Asthma is characterized by increased responsiveness of the tracheobronchial tree to multiple stimuli, leading to narrowing of the air passages with resultant dyspnea, cough, and wheezing.

HP:0002108.name: Spontaneous pneumothorax
HP:0002108.definition: Pneumothorax occurring without traumatic injury to the chest or lung.

HP:0002119.name: Ventriculomegaly
HP:0002119.definition: An increase in size of the ventricular system of the brain.

HP:0002126.name: Polymicrogyria
HP:0002126.definition: Polymicrogyria is a congenital malformation of the cerebral cortex characterized by abnormal cortical layering (lamination) and an excessive number of small gyri (folds).

HP:0002135.name: Basal ganglia calcification
HP:0002135.definition: The presence of calcium deposition affecting one or more structures of the basal ganglia.

HP:0002149.name: Hyperuricemia
HP:0002149.definition: The concentration of uric acid in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
synonyms: Elevated uric acid level in blood
Increased uric acid level in blood

HP:0002171.name: Gliosis
HP:0002171.definition: Gliosis is the focal proliferation of glial cells in the central nervous system.

HP:0002186.name: Apraxia
HP:0002186.definition: A defect in the understanding of complex motor commands and in the execution of certain learned movements, i.e., deficits in the cognitive components of learned movements.

HP:0002240.name: Hepatomegaly
HP:0002240.definition: Abnormally increased size of the liver.

HP:0002251.name: Aganglionic megacolon
HP:0002251.definition: An abnormality resulting from a lack of intestinal ganglion cells (i.e., an aganglionic section of bowel) that results in bowel obstruction with enlargement of the colon.

HP:0002253.name: Colonic diverticula
HP:0002253.definition: The presence of multiple diverticula of the colon.

HP:0002280.name: Enlarged cisterna magna
HP:0002280.definition: Increase in size of the cisterna magna, one of three principal openings in the subarachnoid space between the arachnoid and pia mater, located between the cerebellum and the dorsal surface of the medulla oblongata.

HP:0002308.name: Chiari malformation
HP:0002308.definition: Chiari malformation consists of a downward displacement of the cerebellar tonsils and the medulla through the foramen magnum, sometimes causing hydrocephalus as a result of obstruction of CSF outflow.

HP:0002323.name: Anencephaly
HP:0002323.definition: Anencephaly is a developmental anomaly characterized by a fetus that has no calvarium, with a lack of most or all of the fetus' brain tissue. Anencephaly belongs to a collective group known as neural tube defects (NTD) and is a result of the neural tube failing to close in its rostral end during fetal development.

HP:0002360.name: Sleep disturbance
HP:0002360.definition: An abnormal pattern in the quality, quantity, or characteristics of sleep.

HP:0002414.name: Spina bifida
HP:0002414.definition: Incomplete closure of the embryonic neural tube, whereby some vertebral arches remain unfused and open. The mildest form is spina bifida occulta, followed by meningocele and meningomyelocele.

HP:0002419.name: Molar tooth sign on MRI
HP:0002419.definition: An abnormal appearance of the midbrain in axial magnetic resonance imaging in which the elongated superior cerebellar peduncles give the midbrain an appearance reminiscent of a molar or wisdom tooth.
synonyms: Molar tooth sign on brain imaging

HP:0002463.name: Language impairment
HP:0002463.definition: Language impairment is a deficit in comprehension or production of language that includes reduced vocabulary, limited sentence structure, or impairments in written or spoken communication. Language abilities are substantially and quantifiably below age expectations.

HP:0002500.name: Abnormal cerebral white matter morphology
HP:0002500.definition: An abnormality of the cerebral white matter.
synonyms: Abnormality of the cerebral white matter

HP:0002514.name: Cerebral calcification
HP:0002514.definition: The presence of calcium deposition within the cerebrum.
synonyms: Abnormal deposits of calcium in the brain

HP:0002538.name: Abnormal cerebral cortex morphology
HP:0002538.definition: Any structural abnormality of the cerebral cortex.

HP:0002617.name: Vascular dilatation
HP:0002617.definition: An abnormal increase in the diameter of an artery or vein, either as a diffuse dilatation or as a localized, sac-like outpouching of the vessel wall (aneurysm).
synonyms: Wider than typical opening or gap

HP:0002621.name: Atherosclerosis
HP:0002621.definition: A condition characterized by patchy atheromas or atherosclerotic plaques which develop in the walls of medium-sized and large arteries and can lead to arterial stenosis with reduced or blocked blood flow.

HP:0002623.name: Overriding aorta
HP:0002623.definition: An overriding aorta is a congenital heart defect where the aorta is positioned directly over a ventricular septal defect, instead of over the left ventricle. The result is that the aorta receives some blood from the right ventricle, which reduces the amount of oxygen in the blood. It is one of the four conditions of the Tetralogy of Fallot. The aortic root can be displaced toward the front (anteriorly) or directly above the septal defect, but it is always abnormally located to the right of the root of the pulmonary artery. The degree of override is quite variable, with 5-95% of the valve being connected to the right ventricle.

HP:0002644.name: Abnormal pelvic girdle bone morphology
HP:0002644.definition: An abnormality of the bony pelvic girdle, which is a ring of bones connecting the vertebral column to the femurs.
synonyms: Abnormal shape of pelvic girdle bone
Abnormality of pelvic girdle bone morphology

HP:0002650.name: Scoliosis
HP:0002650.definition: The presence of an abnormal lateral curvature of the spine.

HP:0002652.name: Skeletal dysplasia
HP:0002652.definition: A general term describing features characterized by abnormal development of bones and connective tissues.

HP:0002659.name: Increased susceptibility to fractures
HP:0002659.definition: An abnormally increased tendency to fractures of bones caused by an abnormal reduction in bone strength that is generally associated with an increased risk of fracture.

HP:0002664.name: Neoplasm
HP:0002664.definition: An organ or organ-system abnormality that consists of uncontrolled autonomous cell-proliferation which can occur in any part of the body as a benign or malignant neoplasm (tumor).

HP:0002666.name: Pheochromocytoma
HP:0002666.definition: Pheochromocytomas (also known as chromaffin tumors) produce, store, and secrete catecholamines. Pheochromocytomas usually originate from the adrenal medulla but may also develop from chromaffin cells in or about sympathetic ganglia. A common symptom of pheochromocytoma is hypertension owing to release of catecholamines.

HP:0002667.name: Nephroblastoma
HP:0002667.definition: The presence of a nephroblastoma, which is a neoplasm of the kidney that primarily affects children.

HP:0002671.name: Basal cell carcinoma
HP:0002671.definition: The presence of a basal cell carcinoma of the skin.

HP:0002719.name: Recurrent infections
HP:0002719.definition: Increased susceptibility to infections as manifested by repeated bouts of infection.

HP:0002721.name: Immunodeficiency
HP:0002721.definition: Failure of the immune system to protect the body adequately from infection, due to the absence or insufficiency of some component process or substance.

HP:0002778.name: Abnormal tracheal morphology
HP:0002778.definition: A structural anomaly of the trachea.

HP:0002783.name: Recurrent lower respiratory tract infections
HP:0002783.definition: An increased susceptibility to lower respiratory tract infections as manifested by a history of recurrent lower respiratory tract infections.

HP:0002804.name: Arthrogryposis multiplex congenita
HP:0002804.definition: Multiple congenital contractures in different body areas.

HP:0002857.name: Genu valgum
HP:0002857.definition: The legs angle inward, such that the knees are close together and the ankles far apart.

HP:0002885.name: Medulloblastoma
HP:0002885.definition: A rapidly growing embryonic tumor arising in the posterior part of the cerebellar vermis and neuroepithelial roof of the fourth ventricle in children. More rarely, medulloblastoma arises in the cerebellum in adults.

HP:0002910.name: Elevated circulating hepatic transaminase concentration
HP:0002910.definition: Elevations of the levels of SGOT and SGPT in the serum. SGOT (serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase) and SGPT (serum glutamic pyruvic transaminase) are transaminases primarily found in the liver and heart and are released into the bloodstream as the result of liver or heart damage. SGOT and SGPT are used clinically mainly as markers of liver damage.

HP:0002967.name: Cubitus valgus
HP:0002967.definition: Abnormal positioning in which the elbows are turned out.

HP:0003119.name: Abnormal circulating lipid concentration
HP:0003119.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of a lipid in the blood circulation.

HP:0003196.name: Short nose
HP:0003196.definition: Distance from nasion to subnasale more than two standard deviations below the mean, or alternatively, an apparently decreased length from the nasal root to the nasal tip.

HP:0003220.name: Abnormality of chromosome stability
HP:0003220.definition: A type of chromosomal aberration characterized by reduced resistance of chromosomes to change or deterioration.

HP:0003782.name: Eunuchoid habitus
HP:0003782.definition: A body habitus that is tall, slim and underweight, with long legs and long arms (i.e., arm span exceeds height by 5 cm or more).

HP:0004322.name: Short stature
HP:0004322.definition: A height below that which is expected according to age and gender norms. Although there is no universally accepted definition of short stature, many refer to "short stature" as height more than 2 standard deviations below the mean for age and gender (or below the 3rd percentile for age and gender dependent norms).

HP:0004327.name: Abnormal vitreous humor morphology
HP:0004327.definition: Any structural anomaly of the vitreous body.

HP:0004349.name: Reduced bone mineral density
HP:0004349.definition: A reduction of bone mineral density, that is, of the amount of matter per cubic centimeter of bones.
synonyms: Decreased bone mineral density Z score
Low solidness and mass of the bones

HP:0005227.name: Adenomatous colonic polyposis
HP:0005227.definition: Presence of multiple adenomatous polyps in the colon.

HP:0005280.name: Depressed nasal bridge
HP:0005280.definition: Posterior positioning of the nasal root in relation to the overall facial profile for age.

HP:0005528.name: Bone marrow hypocellularity
HP:0005528.definition: A reduced number of hematopoietic cells present in the bone marrow relative to marrow fat.

HP:0005584.name: Renal cell carcinoma
HP:0005584.definition: A type of carcinoma of the kidney with origin in the epithelium of the proximal convoluted renal tubule.
synonyms: Cancer starting in small tubes in kidneys

HP:0005930.name: Abnormal epiphysis morphology
HP:0005930.definition: An anomaly of epiphysis, which is the expanded articular end of a long bone that developes from a secondary ossification center, and which during the period of growth is either entirely cartilaginous or is separated from the shaft by a cartilaginous disk.
synonyms: Abnormal shape of end part of bone

HP:0005938.name: Abnormal respiratory motile cilium morphology
HP:0005938.definition: Abnormal arrangement of the structures of the motile cilium.

HP:0006118.name: Shortening of all distal phalanges of the fingers
HP:0006118.definition: Hypoplasia of all of the distal phalanx of finger.
synonyms: Shortening of all outermost bones of the fingers

HP:0006254.name: Elevated circulating alpha-fetoprotein concentration
HP:0006254.definition: The concentration of alpha-fetoprotein in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

HP:0006487.name: Bowing of the long bones
HP:0006487.definition: A bending or abnormal curvature of a long bone.

HP:0006536.name: Airway obstruction
HP:0006536.definition: Obstruction of conducting airways of the lung.

HP:0006970.name: Periventricular leukomalacia
HP:0006970.definition: Periventricular leukomalacia is characterized by diffuse injury of deep cerebral white matter, accompanied in its most severe form by focal necrosis. The neuropathologic hallmarks of PVL are microglial activation and focal and diffuse periventricular depletion of premyelinating oligodendroglia.

HP:0007033.name: Cerebellar dysplasia
HP:0007033.definition: Cerebellar dysplasia (abnormal growth or development) is defined by abnormal cerebellar foliation, white matter arborization, and gray-white matter junction. Cerebellar dysplasia is a neuroimaging finding that describes abnormalities of both the cerebellar cortex and white matter and is associated with variable neurodevelopmental outcome. Dysplasia may globally involve the cerebellum or affect only one cerebellar hemisphere. In addition, cerebellar dysplasia may be associated with cortical/subcortical cysts.

HP:0007686.name: Abnormal pupillary function
HP:0007686.definition: A functional abnormality of the pupil.

HP:0007703.name: Abnormal retinal pigmentation
HP:0007703.definition: Any deviation from the normal pigmentation of the retina.

HP:0007737.name: Spicular pigmentation of the retina
HP:0007737.definition: Pigment migration into the retina in a bone-spicule configuration (resembling the nucleated cells within the lacuna of bone).
synonyms: Bone spicule pigmentation of the retina

HP:0007754.name: Macular dystrophy
HP:0007754.definition: Macular dystrophy is a nonspecific term for retinal degeneration, generally confined to the macula, usually presumed of genetic origin.

HP:0007763.name: Retinal telangiectasia
HP:0007763.definition: Localized, irregular dilatation of small tortuous intraretinal blood vessels.

HP:0007843.name: Attenuation of retinal blood vessels
HP:0007843.definition: Narrowing of the retinal blood vessels, both arterioles and venules.
synonyms: Narrowing of blood vessels in back of eye

HP:0008064.name: Ichthyosis
HP:0008064.definition: An abnormality of the skin characterized the presence of excessive amounts of dry surface scales on the skin resulting from an abnormality of keratinization.

HP:0008386.name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the nails
HP:0008386.definition: Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the nail.

HP:0008443.name: Neuropathic spinal arthropathy
HP:0008443.definition: A progressive disorder of vertebral joint degeneration that occurs in the setting of any condition characterized by decreased afferent innervation, involving loss of deep pain and proprioceptive sensation in the vertebral column. Patients most commonly present with symptoms of lower back pain, sitting imbalance, progressive spinal deformity (usually kyphosis), and an audible clicking sound on changing postures.

HP:0008676.name: Congenital megaureter
HP:0008676.definition: A developmental disturbance with extreme ureteral dilatation.

HP:0009124.name: Abnormal adipose tissue morphology
HP:0009124.definition: An abnormality of adipose tissue, which is loose connective tissue composed of adipocytes.

HP:0009711.name: Retinal capillary hemangioma
HP:0009711.definition: A benign vascular tumor of the retina without any neoplastic characteristics.

HP:0009815.name: Aplasia/hypoplasia of the extremities
HP:0009815.definition: Absence (due to failure to form) or underdevelopment of the extremities.

HP:0009826.name: Limb undergrowth
HP:0009826.definition: Limb shortening because of underdevelopment of one or more bones of the extremities.
synonyms: Hypoplasia involving bones of the extremities

HP:0009830.name: Peripheral neuropathy
HP:0009830.definition: Peripheral neuropathy is a general term for any disorder of the peripheral nervous system. The main clinical features used to classify peripheral neuropathy are distribution, type (mainly demyelinating versus mainly axonal), duration, and course.

HP:0009834.name: Abnormal proximal phalanx morphology of the hand
synonyms: Abnormality of the innermost finger bones of the hand
Abnormality of the proximal phalanges of the hand

HP:0010053.name: Abnormality of the distal phalanx of the hallux
synonyms: Abnormality of the outermost bone of the big toe

HP:0010460.name: Abnormality of the female genitalia
HP:0010460.definition: Abnormality of the female genital system.

HP:0010462.name: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the ovary
HP:0010462.definition: Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the ovary.

HP:0010627.name: Anterior pituitary hypoplasia
HP:0010627.definition: Underdevelopment of the anterior pituitary gland.

HP:0010674.name: Abnormal curvature of the vertebral column
HP:0010674.definition: The presence of an abnormal curvature of the vertebral column.
synonyms: Abnormality of the curvature of the vertebral column

HP:0010783.name: Erythema
HP:0010783.definition: Redness of the skin, caused by hyperemia of the capillaries in the lower layers of the skin.
synonyms: Redness of skin or mucous membrane

HP:0010881.name: Abnormality of the umbilical cord
HP:0010881.definition: An abnormality of the umbilical cord, which is the cord connecting the developing embryo or fetus to the placenta.

HP:0011023.name: Abnormal circulating prostaglandin concentration
HP:0011023.definition: Any deviation from the normal concentration of prostaglandin in the blood circulation.

HP:0011024.name: Abnormality of the gastrointestinal tract
HP:0011024.definition: An abnormality of the gastrointestinal tract.

HP:0011034.name: Amyloid deposition
HP:0011034.definition: Pathologic deposits of specific fibrillar protein aggregates with distinct microscopic properties, particularly affinity for the dye Congo red with typical birefringence.

HP:0011220.name: Prominent forehead
HP:0011220.definition: Forward prominence of the entire forehead, due to protrusion of the frontal bone.

HP:0011355.name: Localized skin lesion
HP:0011355.definition: A lesion of the skin that is located in a specific region rather than being generalized.

HP:0011451.name: Primary microcephaly
HP:0011451.definition: Head circumference below 2 standard deviations below the mean for age and gender at birth.
synonyms: Decreased head circumference present at birth
Small head circumference present at birth

HP:0011457.name: Loss of eyelashes
HP:0011457.definition: This term refers to the loss of eyelashes that were previously present.

HP:0011667.name: Bilateral superior vena cava with bridging vein

HP:0011675.name: Arrhythmia
HP:0011675.definition: Any cardiac rhythm other than the normal sinus rhythm. Such a rhythm may be either of sinus or ectopic origin and either regular or irregular. An arrhythmia may be due to a disturbance in impulse formation or conduction or both.

HP:0011800.name: Midface retrusion
HP:0011800.definition: Posterior positions and/or vertical shortening of the infraorbital and perialar regions, or increased concavity of the face and/or reduced nasolabial angle.

HP:0012210.name: Abnormal renal morphology
HP:0012210.definition: Any structural anomaly of the kidney.
synonyms: Structural anomalies of the renal tract

HP:0012385.name: Camptodactyly
HP:0012385.definition: The distal interphalangeal joint and/or the proximal interphalangeal joint of the fingers or toes cannot be extended to 180 degrees by either active or passive extension.
synonyms: Permanent flexion of the finger or toe

HP:0012387.name: Bronchitis
HP:0012387.definition: Inflammation of the large airways in the lung including any part of the bronchi from the primary bronchi to the tertiary bronchi.

HP:0025142.name: Constitutional symptom
HP:0025142.definition: A symptom or manifestation indicating a systemic or general effect of a disease and that may affect the general well-being or status of an individual.

HP:0030084.name: Clinodactyly
HP:0030084.definition: An angulation of a digit at an interphalangeal joint in the plane of the palm (finger) or sole (toe).

HP:0030157.name: Flank pain
HP:0030157.definition: An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort (such as pricking, throbbing, or aching) and perceived to originate in the flank.

HP:0030853.name: Heterotaxy
HP:0030853.definition: An abnormality in which the internal thoraco-abdominal organs demonstrate abnormal arrangement across the left-right axis of the body.

HP:0032394.name: Mesial parasagittal subcortical heterotopia
HP:0032394.definition: Subcortical heterotopia extending along the mesial aspect of the lateral ventricles, with direct connection to mesial polymicrogyria-like cortex at the anterior and posterior limits of the heterotopia.

HP:0032794.name: Myoclonic seizure
HP:0032794.definition: A myoclonic seizure is a type of motor seizure characterized by sudden, brief (<100 ms) involuntary single or multiple contraction of muscles or muscle groups of variable topography (axial, proximal limb, distal). Myoclonus is less regularly repetitive and less sustained than is clonus.

HP:0040208.name: Elevated CSF biopterin level
HP:0040208.definition: Concentration of biopterin in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) above the upper limit of normal.

HP:0100702.name: Arachnoid cyst
HP:0100702.definition: An extra-parenchymal and intra-arachnoidal collection of fluid with a composition similar to that of cerebrospinal fluid.
synonyms: Fluid-filled sac located in membrane surrounding brain or spinal cord

HP:0100750.name: Atelectasis
HP:0100750.definition: Collapse of part of a lung associated with absence of inflation (air) of that part.
synonyms: Partial or complete collapse of part or entire lung

HP:0410030.name: Cleft lip
HP:0410030.definition: A gap in the lip or lips.

HP:0500026.name: Hypoplasia of the musculature of the pelvis
HP:0500026.definition: Underdevelopment of the musculature of the pelvis.
